# Why Bhakti is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is no broken version of this name to repair. There is a record to preserve: **Bhakti**, exactly as the scholarly convention supports it.

Bhakti has no biography — it is the biography of millions. Its ‘myths’ are the movement’s own history: the Gītā’s canonization of devotion, the Tamil saints’ songs, the Maharashtrian kīrtan, and the global chant of the Hare Krishna movement. The tradition’s foundational stories cluster around the saints themselves — the hagiographies of Mirabai, Tukaram, and the gopīs of Braj.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Bhakti
- **ASCII form:** bhakti
- **Meaning:** "Devotion, loving attachment, faith — worship and piety directed toward the divine, esp. as a religious principle and means of salvation."
- **Domain of influence:** Devotion, Love
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** भक्ति
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 92 of 597

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/ˈbʌkti/` — “BUK-tee”

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Bhakti** lives at [/bhakti/](/bhakti/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/bhakti/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/bhakti/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/bhakti/patterns/).

The displayed form is ASCII-equivalent.

## Where the Name Stood First

Bhakti’s monuments are the great temple-towns it animated — Śrīraṅgam, Kanchipuram, Pandharpur — and the palm-leaf hymnals of the Prabandham. The modern ISKCON temples of a hundred cities are its newest layer. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **4 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** (the devotional movements — vernacular, congregational, and still organizing.); **Music, Arts & Performance** (the kīrtan and the nāma-saṅkīrtana — devotion's music, from Tamil hymns to global chant.); **Mental Health & Emotional Wellness** (loving devotion as emotional discipline — the heart's oldest regulated practice.). The [Resonance File](/bhakti/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
